body.estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\) identifies the causal matrix and \(U=\operatorname{left}_r(M)\) is its row subspace. The recorded estimator is \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}=\operatorname{left}_r(\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}))\) with \(\sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\). The observed-data hybrid \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) reports \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and the deterministic sine frame otherwise, and satisfies \(\sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\). The causal target, the two estimators, and their risk bounds are distinct objects.

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and no estimated treatment nuisance; its expected-risk guarantee follows from matrix-martingale concentration and a deterministic singular-subspace inequality. The hybrid switches deterministically, using that fit when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and the first \(r\) columns of the discrete-sine frame otherwise. On nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect classes, \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\), so the hybrid eventually uses the constant-risk fallback. The blind procedure estimates a clipped row fraction and is controlled only at \(d_{nm}\); because \(d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\) in the same regime, its uniform resolution does not shrink. Simultaneous bands use direct recorded-IPW contrasts and deterministic variance envelopes, not feasible multiplier exactness.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD upper bound under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means. Only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\) is shared: their rowwise matrix-error theorem has its own \(\log^4\) factor, whereas \(b_{nm}\) also has \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) conversion to normalized effect-subspace loss.
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

body.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the IPW entry errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array. Writing \(R^\star_{nm}=\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\), the common expected-loss result is now \(c b_{nm}\le R^\star_{nm}\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\). The explicit observed-data hybrid uses recorded IPW--SVD only when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and otherwise reports a deterministic sine frame. Recorded IPW--SVD separately retains its \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) guarantee and estimator-specific obstruction. Nonemptiness under bounded outcomes forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); at fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio this implies \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\). Thus the honest unresolved minimax gap is from \(b_{nm}\) to a constant, and the uniform blind-resolution radius is nonshrinking in this regime. The rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains a blind-scaling failure witness and HeartSteps II stress design; simultaneous dense-query radii retain a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity factor.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not determine effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment. A constant-propensity causal packing gives the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\). Matrix Freedman gives the larger recorded-IPW radius \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), while the deterministic-frame hybrid gives a uniform \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) upper bound. On every nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect class the loose radius is eventually at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\), so the remaining minimax problem is a \(b_{nm}\)-to-constant gap, not a matched-rate theorem.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, with a concrete observed-data hybrid, a separate IPW-specific obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost remains separate from all subspace scales.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the constant-propensity minimax lower benchmark, the expected recorded-IPW spectral bound, the pathwise sine-frame bound, and the hybrid expected-risk upper in one normalized maximum-row criterion. It records the unresolved estimator-independent rate gap, shows that nonempty fixed-complexity classes make both the spectral and blind radii nonshrinking, retains the explicit Markov witness, and supplies direct finite-sample simultaneous bands with their own family-size inflation.

body.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis analyze separate empirical-row-scaled SVD fits for two low-rank arm means under independent Bernoulli assignment. The only shared feature used here is the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\). Their public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 carry their own \(\log^4\) factor, impose armwise assumptions, and bound matrix-row error. In contrast, \(b_{nm}\) also contains \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the factor \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) converting matrix perturbation to normalized effect-subspace loss. No matched-rate transfer is claimed. Algebraically, arm matrices \(A_1,A_0\) always satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(A_1-A_0)\le\operatorname{rank}(A_1)+\operatorname{rank}(A_0)\). The converse fails even for bounded matrices: with \(s=n\wedge m\), \(C=(B/2)\sum_{t=1}^s e_tf_t^\top\), \(A_0=C\), and \(A_1=C+(B/4)e_1f_1^\top\), both arms have rank \(s\) and entries bounded by \(B\), while their difference has rank one. This is only an algebraic separation; it asserts neither full-class containment nor a rate transfer.

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen give two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise; they inform the perturbation and packing architecture but not the predictable causal class. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi and Sun, Zhu, and Dubin give upper-error results for their own arm or completion models, and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan study Frobenius risk under fixed heterogeneous sampling. Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor arm-mean estimation under exogenous factors. These results do not close the present estimator-independent subspace gap.

Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the predictable IPW martingale reduction, and Tropp supplies the matrix Freedman inequality. Khan and Ugander analyze a different scalar normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are not claims about that method. The direct simultaneous theorem keeps \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) outside \(b_{nm}\). Saved propensities and the Markov omission stress test are operationally relevant to the HeartSteps II consumer described by Spruijt-Metz et al.
body.interpretation: The causal target is \(U=\operatorname{left}_r(\mu^1-\mu^0)\), identified by the conditional mean of the recorded IPW score. Writing \(R^\star_{nm}=\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\), the proved headline is \(c b_{nm}\le R^\star_{nm}\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\). The separate recorded-IPW guarantee is \(\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), and its counterexample is estimator-specific. In a nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, the hybrid endpoint is constant because \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\), whereas \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\); determining the true order between them is the live question. Blind-fit loss and the observed blind-versus-recorded diagnostic resolve total drift only up to the nonshrinking radius \(d_{nm}\). The Markov witness is a HeartSteps II stress design, and simultaneous dense-query bands have a separate entropy multiplier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The matrix-Freedman route controls operator norm and then pays \(\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\) in the deterministic subspace conversion. Bounded outcomes imply \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\) whenever the class is nonempty, so at fixed complexity this recorded-IPW radius cannot shrink and is at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\). The sine-frame hybrid repairs the uniform upper endpoint only to a constant and eventually ignores the data in that regime. The frozen class permits target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes; the accepted construction makes this substantive for IPW--SVD but does not rule out a different estimator with vanishing risk. The blind radius \(d_{nm}\) is likewise at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\), so its uniform diagnostic resolution is nonshrinking. No residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed.
body.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded IPW conditional mean. The proved statistical result is a lower/reference benchmark \(c b_{nm}\) and a constant-risk observed-data hybrid upper \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) in the same expected normalized maximum-row loss. These endpoints are not claimed to match. Recorded IPW--SVD retains its separate \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) bound, and the adaptive endogenous-target witness refutes \(b_{nm}\)-attainment only for that estimator. On nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect classes, the spectral and blind radii are nonshrinking; no unconditional \(b_{nm}\)-scale blind criterion is claimed. The \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for the newly defined blind procedure and a HeartSteps II stress design, not a refutation of a published normalization method. Simultaneous inference is supplied by conservative direct-IPW radii with a separate query-family factor.
